figmaExecutionNotes: Do not add unsupported sections such as pricing, testimonials, news, or form.
Keep the page scrollable from hero onward; load the full landing page, not hero-only.
Use a sticky top banner only if the implementation requires global navigation; do not make the trust strip fixed.
Follow design-system-first spacing and card structure; no one-off decorative layouts.
Maintain brand-safe collaboration/productivity styling with Plus Jakarta Sans headings and Inter body.
Mobile should stack sections vertically, convert all grids to single-column cards where needed, and keep the trust strip readable without horizontal crowding.
Use logo-forward trust treatment as the primary credibility device, with the badge text and customer count clearly visible.

heroStrategy.headline: Elevate Your Team’s Productivity with Zoho Workplace
heroStrategy.subheadline: A Complete Email & Collaboration Suite for Enterprises that Facilitates Unified Communication.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a full-width orange hero with a premium mesh-gradient base, subtle grid lines, and soft-shadow enterprise cards layered over it. Keep the headline large and left-aligned on the hero, while the right side features a stacked product montage inside a clean desktop frame. Place a trust strip with the 100,000+ businesses proof directly under the hero content, and ensure the CTA uses Techjockey orange. This composition feels enterprise-grade, proof-led, and visually distinct without relying on a generic split layout.

repetitionBreakers: Hero uses split product montage with orange brand block, while trust is a compact logo grid instead of a form.
Product section 1 uses tabs-with-preview for core collaboration capabilities; product section 2 uses split-panel-list for growth and customization.
Integrations are rendered as compact app tiles, not a feature grid, to reset rhythm after proof-heavy sections.
Testimonials use a spotlight plus 3-card grid rather than another centered content block.
Final CTA is a distinct floating card with a product reminder and a single full-width mobile CTA.
blueprint.pageTitle: Zoho Workplace for Enterprises | Unified Email & Collaboration Suite
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore Zoho Workplace for enterprises: unified email, chat, docs, meetings, and secure collaboration with trusted logos, real-time workflows, integrations, and a clear Get started CTA.

sections.backgroundTreatment: solid brand field with subtle diagonal panel overlay and faint dashboard grid
sections.designNote: Content-first split hero that answers what Zoho Workplace is, who it is for, and what to do next. Left side carries the headline, subheadline, short benefit chips, and a solid orange Get started CTA; right side shows a premium browser-framed product montage of Mail, Chat, Writer, Meetings, and Drive. Keep the product visual layered inside one coherent desktop frame, not as raw screenshots.

Place trust immediately after the hero as a prominent proof band. Use a static 3-6 logo grid with the 100,000+ businesses stat and the line 'Trusted by 100,000+ Businesses Globally'. If exact customer logos are unavailable, convert this to a metric strip with secure-email, remote-work, and productivity stats. Keep the band compact and enterprise-formal.

Use the first product block as a high-focus workflow canvas with tabs for Mail, Chat, Docs, Meetings, and Storage. The preview panel should show a browser-framed app scene that changes with the selected tab, while the tab list acts like the decision layer. This section should emphasize the key click-driving features: unified workspace, real-time collaboration, anywhere access, and Zia AI. The next product block should switch to split-panel-list with an alternating visual/text rhythm to cover business growth, customization, and connected apps without repeating the same card pattern.

Use a clean 4-card benefit grid with short enterprise-oriented reasons to buy through Techjockey: guided selection, migration assistance, enterprise-grade support, and plan clarity. Keep cards compact and icon-led, using the same radius, shadow, and border style as the rest of the page. This is a credibility support section, not a sales pitch.

Present one highlighted pricing card rather than a comparison table, since the input only provides a single plan. The card should feel like a purchase summary with included benefits, storage, device support, and migration assistance. Use the same solid accent CTA button and avoid overcomplicating this section with multi-column pricing noise.

Use a 3-card testimonial grid with a spotlight lead quote above or beside it, drawing from the most outcome-driven quotes. Keep the cards consistent with the enterprise style: author, role, company line, and a short quote. Because there are 5 testimonials, the layout should feel proof-rich but controlled, not carousel-heavy.

Use a floating lead card as the final conversion point, paired with a compact product reminder on the side. Keep the form minimal, visually anchored, and clearly tied to the single CTA text: Get started. Make the button full-width on mobile and use the primary orange at full opacity.

If a news or press strip is used, render it as a tight static logo strip rather than a marquee. Keep it secondary and subdued so it does not compete with the main trust section. If no valid logos are available, omit this section entirely.

blueprint.designPersonality: Structured, credible, and productivity-first. The page should feel like an enterprise operating system: clean grid alignment, generous whitespace, strong logo proof, layered product visuals, and confident orange-led CTAs. It should avoid playful clutter and instead communicate scale, reliability, and unified communication.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a polished Zoho Workplace product montage on the hero right side: overlapping email, chat, document, meeting, and storage UI shells inside a clean desktop mockup. Add small floating collaboration chips like Mail, Chat, Docs, Meetings, and Secure Access. The proof bar beneath the hero should feature a wide logo strip of trusted enterprise brands and a clear 100,000+ businesses stat. Feature sections can use icon-led cards, compact app tiles, and integration badges rather than lifestyle imagery.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long and enterprise-focused, so 40px keeps it confident without overcrowding the split hero layout.

colours.colourReason: Techjockey brand colors lock the palette: orange is the primary hero and CTA color, white and soft grey support the layout, and charcoal provides readable contrast. This creates a distinct, brand-tied identity without borrowing generic SaaS gradients.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Full-width top banner with brand logo, large headline, short supporting paragraph, and a compact benefit list beneath; primary conversion appears immediately after the hero in a separate form block rather than inside the banner.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Single-column editorial flow: hero banner, lead form card, then stacked content sections with repeated headline + description + feature grid patterns; emphasis on vertical progression over dense multi-column storytelling.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Simple boxed cards with clear borders or subtle elevation, rounded corners implied; content-first styling with minimal ornamentation and strong text hierarchy over imagery.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA is singular and high-visibility near the top; secondary conversion is handled through form submission. Repeated CTAs are limited, with the page favoring one dominant action per stage.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing module evident in the reference structure.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not visible in the provided reference, but the page structure suggests a standard low-attention footer after long-form content.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Brand/logo-led hero with minimal imagery; visual communication relies on icon bullets and structural contrast rather than large product visuals or media panels.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Sequential long-form sections with repeated pattern: section title, short explanatory paragraph, then feature lists or feature cards. Designed for scanning and progressive disclosure rather than a dense spec sheet.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead-capture card placed directly under the hero; vertically stacked fields with hidden tracking inputs and a single submit action. Form is treated as a separate conversion module with strong prominence.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, utility-driven presentation with no visible motion system in the reference HTML.
designNotes: Optimize for lead generation by separating persuasion and conversion into distinct blocks.
Use strong typographic hierarchy and short, benefit-led bullets.
Keep sections modular and repetitive for fast scanning on long pages.
Favor clean whitespace and simple cards over complex interactive components.
If media is added, keep it secondary to the message and form conversion flow.

blueprint.heroFormBgRule: MANDATORY: Use heroBackgroundVideo as full-bleed autoplay muted loop video behind everything

mustHaveMoments: Fixed sticky top trust strip featuring 'Trusted by 100,000+ Businesses Globally' and brand/logo proof cues
Immediate hero with clear product value proposition and one primary CTA: Get Started / Free Trial
Logo-led proof block near the top before deeper feature storytelling
Benefit-driven feature section explaining unified workspace, real-time collaboration, anywhere access, and AI productivity
Pricing/inclusion card highlighting enterprise-grade email, migration assistance, storage, and device support
Testimonials section with role-based enterprise credibility
Integration section with recognizable app categories and Zoho ecosystem references
avoidPatterns: Do not use a form in the hero unless the page explicitly requires one
Do not leave empty black space or unfinished right-side hero layouts
Do not use irrelevant media or generic stock visuals that do not match collaboration/email software
Do not overcomplicate with too many CTAs or competing conversion paths
Do not make the top banner non-sticky if used
Do not rely on imagery over proof; logos and trust cues must dominate
Do not present mismatched content blocks or unrelated feature sections
designStrategy.reasoning: This page is a single-product lead-gen landing page for an enterprise collaboration suite, so the design should move quickly from value proposition to proof to feature validation. The audience is enterprise/business buyers who are solution-aware, so they need clarity, credibility, and low-friction conversion rather than exploratory storytelling. Because the strongest trust signal is logos, the page should prioritize a sticky trust strip and logo-first proof treatment near the top. The structure should remain product-led with balanced density: concise hero, stacked explanation sections, pricing/inclusions, testimonials, and integrations. A centered hero keeps the message clean and avoids unnecessary form complexity, while a strong primary CTA supports conversion without competing actions.
